_README.purpose: Hand-built retrieval eval set for the CAT prep RAG pipeline.
_README.method: Each question was written AFTER reading a real chunk in the indexed corpus, so the ground truth is verified to exist rather than assumed. Questions are phrased the way a CAT aspirant would ask them, not as keyword queries copied from the source text.

fields.section: CAT section this belongs to (QA / DILR / VARC / GK)
fields.question: the natural-language query issued to the retriever
fields.must_contain_any: content check - a retrieved chunk must contain at least one of these strings (case-insensitive) for the item to count as a content hit. Kept deliberately short and non-verbatim so the check rewards finding the right MATERIAL, not string-matching the question.
fields.expected_source_any: source check - path fragments; a hit means at least one retrieved chunk came from one of these documents. Multiple entries are allowed because the same concept is legitimately taught in several books.

_README.metrics: hit@k is reported separately for the content check and the source check. Content hit rate is the primary number: it measures whether the retrieved context could actually answer the question.
